summary: HH:MM:SS countdown set over a dot grid; changed digits roll over as their tile reprints, the last ten seconds turn red and zero bursts.

attributes.name: seconds
attributes.description: Starting duration in seconds (8049 is 2 h 14 min 9 s); a negative value counts as zero. Observed: a change restarts the countdown. `restart()` without an argument also reads it.

attributes.name: loop
attributes.description: Presence attribute. Restarts from `seconds` 1.6 s after reaching zero.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Text above the digits; it also names the timer. Observed.

events.name: done
events.description: Fires once when the countdown reaches zero.

methods.description: Starts again from `seconds`, or from the `seconds` attribute when omitted, and updates the end time in the header. A negative duration counts as zero.

accessibility: The digits are text in the monospace font with tabular figures, inside an element with `role="timer"` named by the label through `aria-labelledby`. A timer is not a live region, so the seconds are not announced; the dot canvas is `aria-hidden`.
The header shows the end time as text, for example `at 4:30 PM`.
motion: With reduced motion digits change without rolling and their tiles do not reprint, the colons do not pulse, the urgent tiles do not pulse and no sparks are drawn.
notes: The countdown runs against the wall clock from the moment it connects, so it keeps time while off-screen.

`done` comes from a timer set for zero, so it fires on time while the element is off-screen (the burst only plays on screen). The timers stop while the element is removed from the page and resume when it is inserted again.
Between digit changes the loop sleeps until the next whole second instead of drawing every frame; during the last ten seconds it animates continuously.
`seconds` and `label` are observed; changing `seconds` restarts the countdown.

data.note: Set the duration in `seconds` or call `restart(seconds)`. Without it a demo countdown of 2 h 14 min 9 s runs.
